description: Potential crash in store-stats when the store is empty. compute-store-stats returns an alist without tag-distribution or ref-distribution keys if total-blocks is 0, causing cdr to be called on #f.
code_snippet:
(let ([tag-dist (cdr (assq 'tag-distribution stats))])
     (display "Tag Distribution:\n")
     (let ([tags (list-sort
                  (lambda (a b) (> (cdr a) (cdr b)))
                  (hashtable-map tag-dist cons))])
suggested_fix: Add a check for the existence of the keys or ensure compute-store-stats returns empty distributions. Example: (let ([tag-dist (cond [(assq 'tag-distribution stats) => cdr] [else '()])]))

description: hash->hex uses string-set! on a string that may be immutable. It is created via a redefined make-string which uses list->string; in many Scheme implementations (like Racket), list->string produces immutable strings.
code_snippet:
(let* ([len (bytevector-length hash)]
       [hex-chars (make-string (* len 2) #\0)])
      (let loop ([i 0])
           (when (< i len)
                 (let ([byte (bytevector-u8-ref hash i)])
                      (string-set! hex-chars (* i 2) (int->hex-digit (quotient byte 16)))
                      (string-set! hex-chars (+ (* i 2) 1) (int->hex-digit (remainder byte 16)))
                      (loop (+ i 1)))))
suggested_fix: Use the standard make-string (ensure it's not shadowed) which usually creates mutable strings, or use a bytevector and then convert to string, or use string-append/format to build the hex string.

description: fold-type-string extracts a substitution from the context but fails to apply it to the typed-result, contradicting the intent stated in the comment and likely displaying an un-unified/internal type representation.
code_snippet:
(if (and (pair? context)
         (pair? (car context))
         (eq? (caar context) 'substitution))
    ;; Extract and apply substitution to get final type
    (let ([subst (cadar context)])
         (write typed-result)
         (newline))
suggested_fix: Call a type substitution application function (e.g., apply-substitution) on typed-result before writing it. Example: (write (apply-substitution typed-result subst))

description: test-session-state assumes all session fields ('name, 'tier, 'login-time) are always present in the alist returned by read-session. If any are missing, assq returns #f and cdr will raise an exception.
code_snippet:
(display (format "  Name: ~a
" (cdr (assq 'name session))))
(display (format "  Tier: ~a
" (cdr (assq 'tier session))))
(display (format "  Login time: ~a
" (cdr (assq 'login-time session))))
suggested_fix: Use a helper to safely access alist values. Example: (define (session-ref s k) (let ([p (assq k s)]) (if p (cdr p) "unknown")))

description: Redefinition of standard make-string procedure using an inefficient and non-tail-recursive make-list-of. This shadows the built-in optimized make-string and may cause stack overflow for large n.
code_snippet:
(define (make-string n ch)
  (list->string (make-list-of n ch)))

(define (make-list-of n x)
  (if (= n 0)
      '()
      (cons x (make-list-of (- n 1) x))))
suggested_fix: Remove the redefinition and use the built-in make-string. If a custom version is needed, implement it using a loop and string-set! or a tail-recursive list builder.

description: find-broken-refs uses append in a loop to accumulate results. This leads to O(N^2) complexity in the number of broken references, which can be significant in a corrupted large store.
suggested_fix: Accumulate results using cons and reverse the final list at the end of the loop, or use a more efficient list builder.
